about: Curricula and books suggested for purchase. Status and notes are saved per family in the database; edit this file to add suggestions. An item's optional 'status' sets its starting status (considering, buy, bought, skip) until the parent changes it.

items.subject: art
items.title: Art Fundamentals: All-in-One Homeschool Art Curriculum
items.format: Printed book, 325 full-color pages, lay-flat comb binding
items.for: Ellie and Lillie (one book; each works in her own sketchbook)
items.why: Hands-on drawing and color skills that the Core Knowledge Art & Art History block is light on: line, pattern, shape, texture, value, color mixing and theory, positive and negative space, focal point. Short 20–30 minute lessons, each studying real artists.
items.notes: 4.6 stars from 32 reviews; shop has 260 sales. Two reviewers said the binding is weak. Needs only pencils and colored pencils (plus sketchbooks).

items.subject: life
items.title: Philosophy for Kids: 40 Fun Questions That Help You Wonder About Everything!
items.vendor: David A. White (Prufrock Press); any bookstore
items.price: about $12.99 each (Amazon price per Cathy Duffy; check current)
items.for: Ellie and Lillie (one copy each works best)
items.why: Fills the philosophy weeks of the Human Development, Philosophy & Worldviews block (May 10 – Jun 18). 40 discussion lessons in four groups (values, knowledge, reality, critical thinking), each tied to a philosopher, with teaching tips; no philosophy background needed. Pick about 6 questions for the block.
items.notes: Works best as a discussion with a parent; there are no separate student books or answer keys. Neutral: it doesn't promote a particular philosophy. Sequel 'The Examined Life' (about $37) is harder.

items.subject: life
items.title: What Do You Believe? (DK)
items.vendor: DK / Penguin Random House; any bookstore
items.grades: Upper elementary to middle school (publisher doesn't state an age)
items.for: Ellie and Lillie (one copy can be shared)
items.why: Fills the world-religions weeks of the block: Christianity, Islam, Judaism, Hinduism and Buddhism, plus older beliefs, new movements, modern spirituality and atheism, with scriptures, places of worship, food and clothing. Matches the block's goal of comparing worldviews fairly.
items.notes: The publisher describes it as unbiased; I couldn't find an independent review confirming that. For Lillie, Harvard's free Pluralism Project (pluralism.org) adds case studies and essays.
